provenance: LLM-backend-derived + deterministic-checked (Phase 16/17 inverted boundary) — NOT a ship typology config. EFE (FIN-2022-A002) is also the hand-curated SHOWCASE elder-financial-exploitation typology (rendered in full, including the verbatim advisory); this corpus record is the build-recommendation view over its 12 FINANCIAL red flags — the transaction-data signal surface. EFE's 12 BEHAVIORAL red flags (teller-witnessed observations: distress, caregiver coercion, contact-info changes) are observational SAR-narrative indicators, not a transaction-data signal surface, so they are out of scope for the buildable-signal derivation (the showcase typology presents them). The LLM backend EXTRACTED the 12 financial red flags; the deterministic gate GROUNDS each verbatim `flag` in the source md within the red-flag region + checks the cover×data matrix. build_rec follows the cover×data matrix (build_rec_category). Coverage/data values are ILLUSTRATIVE (vision demo).

indicators.flag: An older customer’s account shows sudden and unusual changes in contact information or new connections to emails, phone numbers, or accounts that may originate overseas
indicators.red_flag: Sudden contact-info change / new overseas-linked email-phone-account connections
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C1 (Customer-profile / out-of-pattern transaction monitoring); data D8.

indicators.flag: An older customer with known physical, emotional, and cognitive impairment has unexplainable or unusual account activity.
indicators.red_flag: Out-of-pattern activity on a known-impaired elderly account
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C1 (Customer-profile / out-of-pattern transaction monitoring); data D1.

indicators.flag: An older customer appears distressed, submissive, fearful, anxious to follow others’ directions related to their financial accounts, or unable to answer basic questions about account activity.
indicators.red_flag: Distressed / coached customer can't explain own account activity
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D20 (External / lifestyle reference data (utilities, registries, merchant classification)), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: An older customer mentions how an online friend or romantic partner is asking them to receive and forward money to one or more individuals on their behalf or open a bank account for a “business opportunity.”
indicators.red_flag: Romance/online-contact directs receive-and-forward or new-account opening (mule recruitment)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D20 (External / lifestyle reference data (utilities, registries, merchant classification)), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: During a transaction, an older customer appears to be taking direction from someone with whom they are speaking on a cell phone, and the older customer seems nervous, leery, or unwilling to hang up.
indicators.red_flag: Live phone-coached transaction with nervous customer
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D20 (External / lifestyle reference data (utilities, registries, merchant classification)), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: An older customer is agitated or frenzied about the need to send money immediately in the face of a purported emergency of a loved one, but the money would be sent to the account of a seemingly unconnected third-party business or individual.
indicators.red_flag: Urgent emergency-pretext payment to unconnected third-party payee
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D20 (External / lifestyle reference data (utilities, registries, merchant classification)), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A caregiver or other individual shows excessive interest in the older customer’s finances or assets, does not allow the older customer to speak for himself or herself, or is reluctant to leave the older customer’s side during conversations.
indicators.red_flag: Controlling caregiver dominates customer interaction
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D20 (External / lifestyle reference data (utilities, registries, merchant classification)), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: An older customer shows an unusual degree of fear or submissiveness toward a caregiver, or expresses a fear of eviction or nursing home placement if money is not given to a caretaker.
indicators.red_flag: Fear/submission toward caregiver tied to coerced payments
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D20 (External / lifestyle reference data (utilities, registries, merchant classification)), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: The financial institution is unable to speak directly with the older customer, despite repeated attempts to contact him or her.
indicators.red_flag: Customer unreachable despite repeated FI contact attempts
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a customer whose KYC record shows integrity gaps or non-cooperation â overdue EDD documents, refused or evasive responses to information requests, or unresolved inconsistencies â escalating when cooperation failures persist past defined deadlines.
build_logic.source: case-management / KYC remediation system + customer correspondence log
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert â AML analyst review & EDD gate

indicators.flag: A new caretaker, relative, or friend suddenly begins conducting financial transactions on behalf of an older customer without proper documentation.
indicators.red_flag: Undocumented new third party transacting on elderly account
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C16 (Third-party / nominee funding & legal-professional channel detection); data D8.

indicators.flag: An older customer’s financial management changes suddenly, such as through a change of power of attorney, trust, or estate planning vehicles, to a different family member or a new individual, particularly if such changes appear to be done under undue influence, coercion, or forgery or the customer has diminished cognitive abilities and is unable to agree to or understand the consequences of the new arrangement.
indicators.red_flag: Sudden PoA/trust/estate-control transfer under undue influence
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag an entity exhibiting shell or front-company markers â opaque or circular beneficial ownership, shared registered addresses or directors, recent incorporation with no observable operations â escalating when nominees or addresses recur across a cluster of related entities.
build_logic.window: rolling 90 days over the ownership/address graph
build_logic.source: corporate registry + KYC beneficial-ownership records + entity-resolution graph
build_logic.route: Tier-2 network alert â AML investigations gate

indicators.flag: An older customer lacks knowledge about his or her financial status, or shows a sudden reluctance to discuss financial matters.
indicators.red_flag: Customer unaware of / suddenly reluctant to discuss finances
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a customer whose KYC record shows integrity gaps or non-cooperation â overdue EDD documents, refused or evasive responses to information requests, or unresolved inconsistencies â escalating when cooperation failures persist past defined deadlines.
build_logic.source: case-management / KYC remediation system + customer correspondence log
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert â AML analyst review & EDD gate

indicators.flag: Dormant accounts with large balances begin to show constant withdrawals.
indicators.red_flag: Dormant high-balance account → sustained constant drawdown
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C6 (Transaction-velocity & dormancy / baseline-deviation monitoring).

indicators.flag: An older customer purchases large numbers of gift cards or prepaid access cards.
indicators.red_flag: High-volume gift-card / prepaid-card purchase
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D4 (Card & merchant-category (MCC) transaction data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a card or account whose merchant-category spend distribution shifts toward high-risk or atypical MCCs for the customer's segment, escalating when spend concentrates in cash-equivalent categories such as gift cards, prepaid, or money-services merchants.
build_logic.window: rolling 60 days vs segment MCC baseline
build_logic.source: card authorization/settlement feed enriched with MCC reference
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert â AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: An older customer suddenly begins discussing and buying CVC.
indicators.red_flag: Sudden first-time CVC purchase by elderly customer
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D7 (Virtual-currency / blockchain analytics), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: An older customer sends multiple checks or wire transfers with descriptors in the memo line such as “tech support services,” “winnings,” or “taxes.”
indicators.red_flag: Scam-keyword memo lines (tech-support / winnings / taxes) on checks-wires
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D5 (Transaction narrative / free-text fields), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: Uncharacteristic, sudden, abnormally frequent, or significant withdrawals of cash or transfers of assets from an older customer’s account.
indicators.red_flag: Out-of-baseline cash withdrawals / asset transfers
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C6 (Transaction-velocity & dormancy / baseline-deviation monitoring).

indicators.flag: An older customer receives and transfers money interstate or abroad to recipients with whom they have no in-person relationship, and the explanation seems suspicious or indicative of a scam or money mule scheme.
indicators.red_flag: Receive-and-forward to no-relationship interstate/overseas payees (mule pass-through)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C2 (Rapid pass-through / flow-through (receive-and-forward) detection).

indicators.flag: Frequent large withdrawals, including daily maximum currency withdrawals from an ATM.
indicators.red_flag: Repeated daily-max ATM cash withdrawals
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C5 (Cash-intensity / cash-placement anomaly detection); data D2.

indicators.flag: Sudden or frequent non-sufficient fund activity.
indicators.red_flag: Sudden / frequent NSF activity
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C6 (Transaction-velocity & dormancy / baseline-deviation monitoring).

indicators.flag: Uncharacteristic nonpayment for services, which may indicate a loss of funds or of access to funds.
indicators.red_flag: Out-of-pattern nonpayment for services (funds-access loss)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C1 (Customer-profile / out-of-pattern transaction monitoring); data D1.

indicators.flag: Debit transactions that are inconsistent for the older customer.
indicators.red_flag: Out-of-baseline debit transactions
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C1 (Customer-profile / out-of-pattern transaction monitoring); data D4.

indicators.flag: Uncharacteristic attempts to wire large sums of money.
indicators.red_flag: Out-of-pattern large-value wire attempts
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C1 (Customer-profile / out-of-pattern transaction monitoring); data D3.

indicators.flag: Closing of CDs or accounts without regard to penalties.
indicators.red_flag: Penalty-disregarding CD / account closure
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C6 (Transaction-velocity & dormancy / baseline-deviation monitoring).
